note: Ballot page data that isn't in the workbook. After the election, set each measure's status to "passed" or "failed" (and the result fields); the page's heading and result badges follow. Every row is one builder's output for both outcomes, so keep passes and fails parallel: same label, same kind of statement, same sources. Each cite's quote is checked against its page of source/excerpts/{source}.json at build time. Each measure's `read` lists the City documents a voter can open to dig deeper; both measures list the same kinds of document in the same order (no campaign sites).

passes.text: Tax revenue proposed to keep it open

cite.quote: Should voters approve the Sales and Use Tax measure, the resulting revenue is proposed to be allocated to maintain operations at the fire station.
Conversely, if the measure does not pass, the proposed station closure will be reconsidered for Fiscal Year 2028.

passes.text: Tax revenue proposed to keep them

cite.quote: Should voters approve the Sales and Use Tax measure, the resulting revenue is proposed to be allocated to maintain the 21 identified sworn and non-sworn positions.

fails.text: Funded only until the vote result

cite.quote: For FY27, the strategy is to utilize one-time funds to delay the elimination of 21 positions until the outcome of the November 2026 Sales and Use Tax measure is known.
as contained in the City Manager’s FY27 & FY28 Proposed Biennial Budget, and as amended by subsequent Council action

countsCaveat.text: Position counts are from the proposed budget. At adoption on June 23, the Council restored 9 Fire positions and 1 City Manager's Office position for FY2027, paid for with $2.29M of revenue transfers, so the gap didn't change. The motion funds the Fire positions in FY2028 too; its table lists FY2027 amounts only.
